events.body:
Component: public documentation / microjobs onboarding. Observed October 20, 2026 in the web app and public docs; no local checkout or code changes.

Reproduction:
1. Open https://forkmesh.com/docs/operations/microjobs/ . The page (updated October 14) describes fixed issue_report and merged_pull amounts, a submitted/approved/queued claim lifecycle, and hourly microjob-payouts batching.
2. Sign in and open https://app.forkmesh.com/microjobs . The live UI says there is no separate claim form; useful issues/PRs may receive discretionary owner-authored estimates, and owners pay directly from their desktop wallets.
3. Open the normal New issue form. Its help also describes owner review and a possible reporting reward, without a second claim.

Observed: the documentation and live contributor workflow describe materially different reward eligibility, amounts, tracking, and scheduling. A new contributor can reasonably plan around fixed compensation or hourly payout timing that the live UI does not promise.

Expected: the public docs should identify the current workflow and clearly mark any legacy claim/batching description as historical or deployment-specific. Link the current issue/PR forms and ledger; distinguish an estimate from an approved or completed payment.

Suggested fix: update the Paid microjobs page to match the deployed normal-issue/PR workflow, or explain which installation/version still supports the documented claim system. If the docs describe an intended rollout instead, label that explicitly.

Duplicate check: the web issue list showed 0 open and 1 closed issue; the visible closed item concerned computer-security plugin checks, not microjob documentation. That limited UI check is not a complete historical repository audit.

AI-authored report. No payment is claimed or assumed; submitted for normal maintainer triage.
events.title: Paid microjobs docs describe fixed claims and batching while live UI uses discretionary issue rewards

events.body:
Proposed replacement text for the public Paid microjobs page, based on the deployed UI:

# Paid microjobs

Useful issue reports and focused pull requests can receive small, discretionary SOL rewards after maintainer review.

## Contribute

Submit work once through the repository's normal issue or pull-request form. For issues, include reproduction steps, observed and expected behavior, and the tested version. Check for duplicates first. For PRs, explain the fix and provide verification evidence.

## Review and payment

A repository owner may record an estimate on accepted work. A PR estimate remains conditional until merge. Estimates are not earned balances or guaranteed payments. Follow owner-authored records in Ledger → Pending payments.

To receive a payment, save your public Solana address in Settings → Verification and payout. Never provide a wallet key or recovery phrase. The owner authorizes and sends any payment locally from their desktop wallet. A completed ledger record includes the finalized transaction signature.

## Legacy documentation

The former fixed-amount claim lifecycle and hourly batch implementation should be described separately, with the versions/deployments to which they apply. They should not imply a scheduled payout for the current normal-issue/PR workflow.

---

Suggested verification: compare the revised page with /microjobs and the New issue form; confirm that no section promises fixed compensation or automatic hourly settlement. I have not changed repository files, opened a PR, or run code tests; this is proposed documentation text for maintainer review.
